headline: Iran's Guards claim missile and drone strikes on Bahrain, targeting US facilities
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced missile and drone strikes on Bahrain, hitting US forces' residential buildings and weapons support warehouses. Bahrain had issued a shelter warning.
details: Iran's Revolutionary Guards announced on Tuesday that they had carried out missile and drone strikes on Bahrain. This declaration came after the Gulf country urged its citizens to take shelter following the sounding of a siren.

Iranian state television IRIB quoted the Guards, detailing that the targets included several weapons support warehouses, a satellite communications center, and the residential building for US forces in Bahrain.

headline_marked: Trump says US [[taking over Strait of Hormuz]], demands 20% fee for protection
headline: Trump says US taking over Strait of Hormuz, demands 20% fee for protection
summary: President Donald Trump announced the US will act as the 'Guardian of the Hormuz Strait' and seek reimbursement for protecting cargo in the vital waterway.
details: US President Donald Trump declared that the United States is "taking over" the Strait of Hormuz and will be paid for protecting the vital waterway. He stated the US will be known as the 'Guardian of the Hormuz Strait' and will be reimbursed at a rate of 20% on all shipped cargo.

Trump also announced the reinstatement of the US blockade of Iranian shipping in the Gulf. This comes as Washington and Tehran engage in a cycle of attacks, with the US military reporting hits on dozens of targets and Iran's Revolutionary Guards striking targets in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, and Oman.

Iran's military command has strongly rejected the US claims, insisting it will not allow the United States to interfere in the management of the strategic conduit for oil and gas. Tehran has also warned its Gulf neighbors against cooperating with Washington.

The situation has escalated since February, when the US and Israel began their war with Iran. While the Strait was previously free, Tehran subsequently blocked the waterway, which it now views as essential leverage over the US.

Despite the hostilities, Trump indicated that negotiations for a permanent settlement would continue, though he accused Iranian negotiators of reneging on previous agreements. Iran's foreign ministry says the memorandum of understanding forming the basis for talks is now 'in crisis'.

Recent strikes have targeted air defenses, coastal radar systems, and small boats in Iran's south and west. Meanwhile, Jordan's army reported intercepting four Iranian missiles, and Kuwaiti forces intercepted other hostile aerial targets.
